sources.entry: scipy - Fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python.

summary.one_liner: SciPy is an open-source Python library of fundamental algorithms and numerical routines for mathematics, science, and engineering, built to work with NumPy arrays.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes SciPy as covering modules for statistics, optimization, integration, linear algebra, Fourier transforms, signal and image processing, and ODE solvers. It states the routines are built to work with NumPy arrays and include efficient numerical routines such as numerical integration and optimization. The README links to website, documentation, a development docs version, a forum, Stack Overflow, source code, contributing and bug report pages, and a citation guide. It also points to a Tidelift channel for reporting security vulnerabilities. The README is mainly project-level information and a contributor call; it does not walk through API usage in detail.
how_to_run: See the installation guide linked from the README (the README itself gives no install commands).
notable: Covers statistics, optimization, integration, linear algebra, Fourier transforms, signal and image processing, and ODE solvers in one package
Built to work with NumPy arrays
Free and open-source, described as running on all popular operating systems
Has a public contributor guide and a list of ways to contribute beyond code
caveats: The README gives no install commands; it defers to an external install guide
Security vulnerabilities are reported through Tidelift, per the linked docs
